content.title: Pay for an enterprise order
content.description: A Buyer or Procurement Manager settles an order by either submitting a purchase order against the account credit line or paying by corporate card, with PO and card-field validation, credit and per-order card limits, consecutive-failure lockout behavior, and plain-text card-storage prohibition enforced before payment can proceed.
content.summary: Complete payment by PO or corporate card.
content.value: Collects payment using enterprise controls that prevent uncollectible or insecure orders.
criteria: Payment offers exactly two methods: Purchase Order (on account) and Corporate Card.
Purchase Order payment requires a PO number matching `PO-` followed by 6 digits and uses Net 30 terms.
Purchase Order payment is blocked when the order total exceeds the account's available credit of $150,000, and the buyer is directed to use a corporate card or contact the account manager.
Corporate Card accepts Visa, Mastercard, and Amex; validates the card number with a Luhn check; requires a future expiry; and requires CVV of 3 digits, or 4 for Amex.
Corporate Card payment is limited to $10,000 per order, with an above-limit message directing the buyer to use a purchase order.
After 3 consecutive card-authorization failures, the card form is locked for 15 minutes and a support contact is shown.
Card data is never stored in plain text.

content.title: Approve or reject a high-value enterprise order
content.description: A Procurement Manager reviews pending approval requests for orders above the spending threshold, sees the requester and total context, approves to place the order or rejects with a sufficiently detailed reason, is prevented from acting on their own request, and leaves an auditable decision record.
content.summary: Review and decide high-value order requests.
content.value: Enforces spending policy, segregation of duties, and auditability on high-value purchases.
criteria: Orders whose total, including tax and delivery, exceeds $25,000 require Procurement Manager approval.
Submitting for approval creates a request ID in the format `REQ-` followed by 5 digits and stores status `Pending Approval`, requester name, total, and submitted time.
The Approvals page lists all requests with their status, and pending requests expose `Approve` and `Reject` actions to approvers.
Rejecting a request requires a reason of at least 10 characters, changes the request status to `Rejected`, and shows the reason to the requester.
Approving a request changes its status to `Approved` and places the order, generating an order number.
An approver cannot approve or reject their own request; those actions are hidden and the message `You cannot approve your own request` is shown.
Every approval decision records approver, timestamp, and reason.

content.title: Submit an over-limit enterprise order for approval
content.description: A Buyer submits an order whose total including tax and delivery exceeds the per-order spending limit into the approval workflow, sees the over-limit warning on order review, uses Submit for Approval instead of direct placement, and receives a tracked pending request rather than an immediate order.
content.summary: Route an over-limit order into approval.
content.value: Prevents direct purchase above the spending threshold while preserving the order as an approval request.
criteria: A Buyer's per-order spending limit is $25,000, and orders whose total including tax and delivery exceeds that amount require approval.

On order review for an over-limit order, the buyer sees the banner `This order exceeds the $25,000 spending limit and requires Procurement Manager approval.` and the primary action becomes `Submit for Approval` instead of `Place Order`.
Submitting for approval creates a request ID in the format `REQ-` followed by 5 digits with status `Pending Approval`, requester name, total, and submitted time.

content.title: Place an enterprise device order
content.description: A Buyer or Procurement Manager reviews the full order before submission, can return from review to edit shipping, delivery, or payment details, places the order directly when approval is not required, gets duplicate-submission protection on the action itself, sees confirmation details and acknowledgement email timing on success, and gets product-specific recovery choices when stock allocation fails at placement.
content.summary: Submit a quote as a committed order.
content.value: Turns a reviewed quote into a confirmed revenue-bearing order with clear success and failure handling.
criteria: Orders at or below $25,000 are placed directly without approval.

Before final submission, order review shows all lines with configuration, quantity, discounted unit price, and services; ship-to site; delivery method and estimated delivery date; payment method as PO number or card brand plus last 4 digits; and hardware subtotal, volume discount, services, tax, delivery, and order total.
The review screen allows editing ship-to site, delivery method and estimated delivery date, and payment method by returning to FR-5 or FR-6.
`Place Order` is disabled after the first click to prevent double submission.

Successful placement shows an order number in the format `NT-` followed by 8 characters, shows the PO number when paid by PO, shows estimated delivery date and order total, offers `Print Order`, and sends an acknowledgement email within 5 minutes.
If stock allocation fails for a constrained item at placement, the buyer sees an error naming the affected product with options `Remove item and retry` or `Return to quote`.

content.title: Arrange shipping and delivery for an enterprise order
content.description: A Buyer or Procurement Manager chooses a saved site or enters a new ship-to location, completes the required address and optional tax fields for a supported country, is blocked on invalid country-specific postal or exemption formats, selects an eligible delivery method, and receives tax, delivery cost, and estimated delivery date calculations that account for discounts, services, backorder lead time, geography, and order size.
content.summary: Capture ship-to details and delivery method.
content.value: Ensures the order can be delivered with correct tax and fulfillment charges.
criteria: Ship-to selection offers the account's saved sites, such as `HQ — San Jose` and `EU Hub — Frankfurt`, and also allows entry of a new site.
Required ship-to fields are company name, attention (recipient name), street address line 1, city, state/province, postal code, country, and phone number.
Optional ship-to fields are street address line 2 and tax exemption certificate number.
Supported countries are United States, Canada, United Kingdom, Germany, France, Japan, and India; an invalid postal code format for the selected country hard-blocks submission.

Tax is 8.25% of discounted hardware plus services; a tax exemption certificate matching `EXM-` followed by 6 digits sets tax to $0.00; any other format shows `Invalid exemption certificate format (EXM-123456)` and blocks submission.

Delivery methods are Standard Ground (5–7 business days, free if hardware subtotal ≥ $5,000 otherwise $49, all countries), Expedited (2–3 business days, $199 per order, United States and Canada), and White-Glove Deployment (10 business days, $75 per device, United States only and 25 or more devices on the order).
Estimated delivery date is calculated as today plus the quote's longest backorder lead time, if any, plus the selected delivery window, counted in business days.

content.title: Build and save an enterprise procurement quote
content.description: A Buyer or Procurement Manager assembles a quote from account-available catalog products, sees product-card status and quote-line pricing details including discounts and stock lead time, can save the quote as a dated quote record, and can proceed to checkout only when the quote contains orderable, non-EOL lines.
content.summary: Assemble and save a priced quote.
content.value: Creates a reusable, accurately priced quote that can move into checkout.
criteria: Catalog product cards show product name, category in Laptop/Workstation/Tablet/Accessory, image, starting price, and availability as `In Stock`, `Backorder — ships in N days`, or `End of Life`.
Configurable products (laptops and workstations) expose `Configure`, while non-configurable products (accessories and tablets) expose `Add to Quote`.
End-of-life products show an `End of Life` badge, cannot be added to a quote, and show the recommended replacement product by name.

Each quote line shows product name, configuration summary (processor, memory, storage, OS), editable quantity with minimum 1 and maximum 500, list unit price, volume-discounted unit price, selected services, and line total.
Volume pricing applies only to hardware unit price, with discounts of 0% for quantities 1–9, 5% for 10–49, 10% for 50–99, and 15% for 100+.

Quote summary shows hardware subtotal (list), volume discount, services total, subtotal, tax as `TBD` until a shipping address is entered, delivery as `TBD` until a delivery method is chosen, and quote total.
If line quantity exceeds available stock, the line shows `Backorder: N units ship in X days`; backorders do not block checkout but do push out the estimated delivery date.
`Save Quote` generates a quote number in the format `Q-` followed by 6 digits and shows `Valid until` a date 30 calendar days from today.
An empty quote shows `Your quote is empty` with a `Browse Catalog` link and no checkout button.
`Proceed to Checkout` is disabled while the quote contains any end-of-life product, and those lines must be removed.

content.title: Select per-device services and support
content.description: A Buyer or Procurement Manager augments each hardware line with warranty, support, deployment, and tagging services priced per device, subject to single-tier warranty selection and OS- and quantity-based eligibility rules that disable or remove incompatible services with an explanatory message.
content.summary: Add support and deployment services per device.
content.value: Captures service attach revenue while ensuring service selections remain valid for the device and quantity ordered.
criteria: Per-device service options are Standard Warranty (1 year, Included, Default), ProSupport (3 years, next business day onsite, $149), ProSupport Plus (3 years, includes accidental damage, $249), Windows Autopilot Enrollment ($12), Custom OS Imaging ($15), and Asset Tagging ($5).
Only one warranty tier may be selected per line.
Windows Autopilot Enrollment is available for Windows 11 Pro only and is disabled for Ubuntu.
Custom OS Imaging requires line quantity of 10 or more, and if quantity drops below 10 while it is selected the service is removed with the message `Custom OS Imaging requires 10 or more devices`.

content.title: Configure a device for a quote
content.description: A Buyer or Procurement Manager configures a laptop or workstation by selecting processor, memory, storage, and operating system options, sees the running unit price update as choices change, encounters disabled or auto-corrected states when compatibility rules are violated, and adds a configuration to the quote with a quantity constrained between 1 and 500.
content.value: Produces orderable device configurations with immediate pricing and visible compatibility enforcement.
criteria: Processor choices are Core Ultra 5, Core Ultra 7, and Core Ultra 9, with price adjustments of +$0, +$250, and +$550 respectively.
Memory choices are 16 GB, 32 GB, and 64 GB, with price adjustments of +$0, +$200, and +$500 respectively.
Storage choices are 512 GB, 1 TB, 2 TB, and 4 TB, with price adjustments of +$0, +$150, +$350, and +$700 respectively.
Operating system choices are Windows 11 Pro and Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, with price adjustments of +$0 and −$50 respectively.
Running unit price updates immediately as configuration options change.

64 GB memory requires Core Ultra 9; if the processor is downgraded while 64 GB is selected, memory is automatically changed to 32 GB and the message `64 GB memory requires Core Ultra 9 — memory changed to 32 GB` is shown.
4 TB storage is available on Workstation products only; on laptops the option is disabled with the reason `Workstation only`.
Incompatible options are shown disabled with the reason visible next to them and are never silently hidden.
Configured-device quantity must be between 1 and 500 before `Add to Quote`.
